title: Pesher Habakkuk (1QpHab), columns VI-XIII
source: Israel Museum photograph of scroll 1QpHab (Digital Dead Sea Scrolls) + ETCBC dss transcription (Abegg; CC BY-NC 4.0) + English of W. H. Brownlee, BASOR 112 (1948), public domain
description: Columns VI to XIII of the Habakkuk Commentary from Qumran Cave 1, on Habakkuk 1:16 to 2:20: the Teacher of Righteousness, the Wicked Priest, the Day of Atonement and the end of days, each column shown on the Israel Museum's photograph of the scroll.
introduction:
The Habakkuk Commentary (Pesher Habakkuk, 1QpHab) is one of the seven scrolls found in Qumran Cave 1 in 1947. It quotes the first two chapters of the book of Habakkuk a phrase at a time and explains each quotation with the word pesher ("its meaning"), applying the prophet's words to the community's own time: the Teacher of Righteousness, the Wicked Priest, the Man of the Lie, and the Kittim, a foreign power usually identified with Rome. The scroll is about 1.48 m long and is kept in the Shrine of the Book at the Israel Museum, Jerusalem (inv. 95.57/28). On the evidence of its handwriting it is usually dated to the late first century BCE.

This entry gives columns VI to XIII, the second half of the scroll (Habakkuk 1:16 to 2:20); columns I to V are in the previous entry. Column VII explains that God made known to the Teacher of Righteousness "all the mysteries of the words of His servants the prophets"; columns VIII to XII describe the Wicked Priest, his pursuit of the Teacher on the Day of Atonement and his punishment; column XIII, of four lines, ends the work, and the rest of the last sheet is ruled but left blank. Each section is one column. The Hebrew is the scroll's own text with its column and line numbers, from the transcription of Martin G. Abegg Jr. and colleagues in the ETCBC "dss" dataset. Square brackets mark letters lost from the leather and restored by the editors; a dot under a letter marks an uncertain reading; ⟨ ⟩ marks letters written above the line; an ellipsis marks lost letters that are not restored.

The English is the complete translation of the scroll by William H. Brownlee, published in December 1948. Brownlee kept the scroll's columns. In his notation a diagonal line (/) marks the start of a new line of the scroll, words in parentheses are his conjectural restorations, a row of dots (shown here as …) is a lacuna, ? marks traces of letters, # marks letters that can be read but not translated, and words between asterisks were moved across a line division. His quotations of Habakkuk are set in italics. Superscript numbers give the lines of the scroll: they stand where each line of the scroll begins in the English, at Brownlee's / marks, checked against the Hebrew line by line.

The photographs are the Israel Museum's own images of the scroll from its Digital Dead Sea Scrolls site, one image per column. The lowest lines of columns VI to XII are broken off along the torn lower edge of the scroll; the transcription restores some of them in square brackets, and Brownlee's English marks them as lacunae.
translator_notes: Brownlee's translation of 1948 predates later work on the scroll; his restorations in parentheses sometimes differ from the restorations in square brackets in the Hebrew transcription.
Footnote numbers in Brownlee's text are omitted. Each printed row of dots is shown as a single ellipsis.
In column XII Brownlee's "(The spoil of the beasts) /" before line 1 renders words he restored at the foot of column XI; line 1 of column XII begins at "he seized".

1the Chittiim; for they gather their wealth with all their loot / 2as fish of the sea; and when it says, “Wherefore, he sacrifies to his net / 3and burns incense to his seine,” its meaning is that they / 4do sacrifice to their standards; and that their battle weapons—these are the / 5object of their reverence.

For thereby his ration is liberal,
And his food is abundant. /

6Its meaning is that they distribute their yoke and / 7their tax-burden—their “food”—upon all the peoples year by year / 8so as to empoverish many lands.

He shall therefore draw his sword continually /
9To slay nations without showing mercy! /

10Its meaning concerns the Chittiim who destroy many with the “sword”: / 11sturdy youths, also old men, women, and even children; for toward the fruit of / 12the womb they do not “show mercy.”

At my watch I stand, /
13And at my post I keep my station,
And stay alert to see what He will say / 14to me
And with what I may respond concerning my contention.
Then the Lord answers / 15(and says,
Write the vision and inscri)be it upon tablets,
That he may run / 16(who reads therefrom).

(Its meaning concerns) …

translation.text:
1And God said to Habakkuk to write the things that were to come upon / 2upon the last generation; but the final phase of the end He did not make known to him. / 3And when it says, “That he may run who reads therefrom,” / 4its meaning concerns the Teacher of Righteousness to whom God has made known / 5all the mysteries of the words of His servants the prophets:

For the vision is still / 6for the appointed time;
It speaks of the end and does not lie.

7Its meaning is that the final end delays and is left for all / 8of which the prophets spoke; for the mysteries of God are to be marvellous.

9Though it lingers, wait for it;
For it surely comes and will not / 10be late.

Its meaning concerns the men of truth, / 11the doers of the Law, whose hands do not slack from the service of / 12the truth when for them the final end delays; for / 13all His summer fruits God will bring into their store-house, just as He decreed / 14for them through the mysteries of His wisdom.

Behold! /
15(His soul within him) * is puffed up—not made straight.*

Its meaning is that they double upon themselves / 16…?…?? ** in their judgment …

translation.text:
1Its meaning concerns all the doers of the Law in the house of Judah whom / 2God will deliver from the house of judgment for the sake of their labor and their “faith” / 3in the Teacher of Righteousness:

Yea wealth, indeed, is treacherous—
A haughty man who does not / 4rest,
Who enlargeth his desire as Sheol;
And he as death is never sated. /
5For gathered unto him are all the nations;
And amassed unto him are all the peoples. /
6Shall not they all take up a parable against him,
And the taunts of satire concerning him, /
7Saying, ‘Woe to him who amasses what is not his!
How long shall he lead himself / 8with extorted pledges?’

Its meaning concerns the wicked priest who / 9was summoned against the name of the truth in the beginning of his assumption of power; and as he ruled / 10in Israel, his heart became lofty, and he abandoned God and “moved treacherously” against the statutes for the sake of / 11“wealth.” He robbed and “amassed” “the wealth” of the men of violence who had rebelled against God! / 12He also took “the wealth” of “the peoples” so as to incur for himself the guilt of transgression; for the ways of / 13abominations he carried out with every impurity of defilement.

Shall not they suddenly arise / 14and exact from thee?
Shall not thy torturers awaken,
And thou become booty for them? /
15Since thou hast plundered many nations,
All the remnant of the peoples shall plunder thee! /

16(The meaning of the passage) concerns the priest who rebelled / 17(and transgressed) against the statutes of (God) … ?????

1his smiting with the penalties of wickedness; while horrible things, diseases / 2and thirst they execute upon him, and acts of vengeance upon his body of flesh. And when / 3it says:

Since thou hast plundered many nations,
All / 4the remnant of the peoples * shall plunder thee *—

its meaning concerns the / 5latest * priests of Jerusalem * who will gather wealth and loot from the spoil of the peoples. / 6But in the last days they will give their wealth with their spoil into the hand of / 7the army of the Chittiim; for they are the “remnant of the peoples.” /

8Because of men’s blood,
And for the violence done to the land,
To the city and all that dwell therein. /

9Its meaning concerns the wi(ck)ed priest—whom, in the sight of the Teacher of / 10Righteousness and the men of his counsel, God gave into the hand of his enemies to abuse / 11with smiting that he might be consumed with bitterness of soul, because he had done evil / 12against His elect.

For the grasper of evil gain for his (hou)se,
That he may put / 13his nest up high

To cut off so many peoples,

To cut off so many peoples,
Thou dost sin against thy soul— /

3it means thus: It is the house of judgment whose / 4judgment * God will give * among “so many peoples”; for from there He will bring it up for judgment, / 5and in their midst He will convict it—, judging it with a fire of brimstone!

1the Lie. And afterward “the knowledge” will be revealed to them as “the waters” of / 2“the sea” for abundance.

Woe to him that gives drink to his neighbor
Venting / 3his wrath to make him drunk too,
So as to gaze upon their festivals! /

4Its meaning concerns the wicked priest who / 5persecuted the Teacher of Righteousness in order to swallow him up in the vexation of / 6“his wrath,” intending him to go into exile. So at the end of the “festival,” on the resting of / 7the Day of Atonement, he appeared in splendor unto them for the purpose of swallowing them up / 8and that they might stumble on that fast day, the sabbath of their resting:

Thou art sated / 9with shame instead of glory;
Drink, thou too, and reel! /
10The cup of the Lord’s right hand comes round to thee,
That shame may be / 11upon thy glory! /

12Its meaning concerns the priest whose “shame” exceeded his “glory”; / 13for he did not circumcise the uncircumcision of his heart; but he walked in the ways of / 14hard drinking—only to add to his thirst! And the “cup” of the wrath of / 15(Go)d will swallow him up, to fur(ther upon him) his (sha)me; and causing pain / 16…?…?…?…

6כאשר זמם לכלות אביונים ואשר אמר מדמי
7קריה וחמס ארץ פשרו הקריה היא ירושלם
8אשר פעל בה הכוהן ⟨הרשע⟩ מעשי תועבות ויטמא את
9מקדש אל וחמס ארץ המה ערי יהודה אשר
10גזל הון אביונים מה הועיל פסל כיא פסל יצרו
11מס[י]כה ומרי שקר כיא בטח יצר יצריו עליהו
12לעשות אלילים אלמים פשר הדבר על כול
13פסלי הגוים אשר יצרום לעובדם ולשתחות
14להםה והמה לוא יצילום ביום המשפט הוי
15ה[אומר ל]ע̣צ הקיצה [עורי לא]ב̣ן דומה
16[הוא יורה הנה הוא תפוש זהב וכסף]
17[וכול רוח אין בקרבו ויהוה בהיכל קודשו]
translation.text:
(The spoil of the beasts) / 1he seized.
Because of the blood of men,
And violence to the land,
To the city and all that dwell therein /

2The meaning of the passage concerns the wicked priest to recompense to him / 3the ill-treatment with which he ill-treated the poor; for “Lebanon,” it is / 4counsel of the community, and “the beasts,” they are the simple ones of Judah, the doers of / 5the Law—this priest shall God condemn to destruction / 6in as much as he plotted to destroy the poor. When it says, “Because of the blood / 7of the city, and violence to the land” its meaning is: “The city”—it is Jerusalem / 8wherein the wicked priest wrought works of abomination and defiled / 9the sanctuary of God; and “violence to the land,”—they are the cities of Judah which / 10robbed the wealth of the poor.

What profits a graven image,
When its maker has carved?
11A molten image and bitterness of falsehood,
When the fashioner of his images trusts therein /
12To make worthless dumb idols?

The meaning of the passage concerns all / 13the idols of the nations which they fashion so that they may worship them and bow down / 14to them; but they will not deliver them on the Day of Judgment!

Alas! /
15(For him who saith) to wood, “Awaken”;
To the lofty stone, “Arise!”
translation.scan_note: Image 1qphab-col-12.jpg (Israel Museum photograph, column XII). Checked on the image: line 1 reads יחתה מדמי אדם וחמס ארץ קריה וכול יושבי בה, line 5 is the short line התורה אשר ישופטנו אל לכלה, line 8 has הרשע written above the line, line 14 reads להםה והמה לוא יצילום ביום המשפט הוי, line 15 survives in part on the torn lower edge (15 lines with text). Column and line numbers of the Hebrew come from the ETCBC/Abegg transcription. The English line numbers mark the point where each line of the scroll begins in Brownlee's translation, at his / marks, and were checked against the Hebrew line by line, so both texts carry the same numbers. Line 11 has no / in Brownlee; its number is placed at “A molten image”, the rendering of מס[י]כה, the first word of line 11.

translation.original_text:
1הס מלפניו כול הרץ פשרו על כול הגוים
2אשר עבדו את האבן ואת העץ וביומ
3המשפט יכלה אל את כול עובדי העצבים
4ואת הרשעים מן הארץ
translation.text:
1Keep silence before him, all the earth! /

Its meaning concerns all the nations / 2who worship “stone” and “wood.” For on the day of / 3judgment, God will destroy in the sea all the worshippers of “wood”; / 4and from off the earth, the wicked! /
translation.scan_note: Image 1qphab-col-13.jpg (Israel Museum photograph, column XIII, the last column). Checked on the image: the column has four lines, the rest of the sheet is ruled but blank: line 1 reads הס מלפניו כול הרץ, a blank space, פשרו על כול הגוים, line 4 reads ואת הרשעים מן הארץ. Column and line numbers of the Hebrew come from the ETCBC/Abegg transcription. The English line numbers mark the point where each line of the scroll begins in Brownlee's translation, at his / marks, and were checked against the Hebrew line by line, so both texts carry the same numbers. Brownlee's / after “all the earth!” does not mark a line of the scroll (line 1 continues with פשרו על כול הגוים); line 2 begins after the / following “nations”.
